output.reason: [ev-463f236bf567] says that RSA certificates with 3072- or 4096-bit keys now use SHA-384 or SHA-512. That behaviour change reaches every environment holding such certificates, and the consequence is fixed as behavior-change. Possible errors from consumers are only a caution ("we don't expect this to be an issue"), so they are not part of what triggers exposure. Joining the resource predicate with an undecidable consumer-support leaf makes the condition narrower than the change: it can never evaluate true. The exposure should therefore be just the Certificate key-size predicate. The evidence does not name the field path, so spec.privateKey.size is taken from the proposals, which is why confidence is low.

correction.statement: From cert-manager 1.17.0, RSA certificates with 3072-bit keys use SHA-384 and those with 4096-bit keys use SHA-512 as the hash algorithm. Exposed environments are those with a Certificate whose RSA private key size is 3072 or 4096; the change takes effect as these keys rotate.
